Our work underscores a particular assembly pathway through lamellar micelles as an effective approach for building up ultrafast mesopore highways toward promising diffusion-related applications.

item.title: JACS: Specific Amino Acid Imaging of Protein Condensates in Live Cells by Stimulated Raman Scattering Microscopy
item.description:
Ruifeng Sun, Ruowei Zhang, Fanghao Hu
Intracellular protein condensates formed by liquid–liquid phase separation have gained increasing attention in recent years due to their key roles in many physiological and pathological processes. However, fluorescence imaging of protein condensates is limited by the bulky fluorescent tags that could perturb the protein localization and interaction. Imaging techniques that can visualize protein condensates in live cells with minimal perturbations remain lacking. Here, we develop a strategy to image intracellular protein condensates by coupling stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy to specific amino acid labeling. Different types of amino acids are found to exhibit distinct incorporation patterns in the live cells. By metabolic labeling of deuterated tyrosine-d4 and arginine-d7, ALS-related fused in sarcoma (FUS) protein condensates can be visualized with a high specificity. In addition, two-color pulse-chase imaging reveals protein translation arrest in FUS condensates under stress conditions. Furthermore, heterogeneous tyrosine phosphorylation is imaged in live cells and FUS condensates based on the Raman blue shift of phosphorylated tyrosine-d4. Thus, our technique to image specific amino acids by SRS provides a new platform to visualize the metabolic turnover and post-translational modifications of protein condensates in live cells with minimal perturbation.

item.title: ACS Nano: Competing Surface Dynamics of Copper Catalyst Particles during Electrochemical Carbon Dioxide Reduction
item.description:
Yifan Chen, Tom Burwell, Madasamy Thangamuthu, Sadegh Ghaderzadeh, Gazi N. Aliev, Haytham E. M. Hussein, Sean Hoggett, Michael W. Fay, et al.
Copper is a powerful catalyst for the electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO2RR), but it faces challenges with selectivity and stability dependent on its structural characteristics. We developed a platform that combines graphitized carbon nanofibers with identical-location transmission electron microscopy (IL-TEM) to study individual copper nanoparticles at the atomic scale under various reaction conditions. Notably, we observed that competing phenomena such as Ostwald ripening, coalescence, selective etching, and Coulomb-explosion-like fragmentation coexist in the same reaction area, with the latter being qualitatively consistent with a charge-driven fission pathway in larger nanoparticles (>10 nm). By tracking uniquely identifiable nanoparticles both individually and in groups, our findings focus on the range of surface-confined restructuring pathways during CO2RR. This contrasts with solution-mediated phenomena, such as dissolution–precipitation, which dominate under open-circuit potential (OCP) and significantly destabilize the catalyst prior to the reaction, highlighting the importance of eliminating this effect. Under CO2RR conditions, Cu nanoparticles are highly sensitive to subtle variations in the support’s nanotexture, defects, and electronic structure, leading to the coexistence of counteracting mechanisms we observed. These observations provide a structural framework for understanding the dynamic behavior of copper-on-carbon catalysts under CO2RR conditions, guiding the development of strategies to improve catalyst stability and performance.

item.title: JACS: Breaking the “Micro-Size Inversion” Paradox via a Surface-Chemistry-Driven Molecular Sieving Membrane for Ambient Lithium–Air Batteries
item.description:
Yiwen Liu, Xiaoya Zhao, Zhang Wen, Bingxuan Du, Yu Shi, Lunjie Qin, Wei Li, Haoshen Zhou, et al.
Lithium–air batteries suffer from moisture-induced parasitic reactions and electrolyte evaporation in ambient air. A fundamental challenge is the “micro-size inversion” paradox, where H2O (0.275 nm) is smaller than O2 (0.346 nm), rendering conventional size-based sieving ineffective. Here, we report a composite membrane composed of polydimethylsiloxane and fluorinated vinyl-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF-VF) to break this selectivity barrier. By grafting 1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorodecyl groups onto a vinyl-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF-V), we establish a surface-chemistry-driven sieving mechanism. This design creates a molecular-level hydrogen-bond-repellent barrier that specifically inhibits polar H2O penetration while maintaining high nonpolar O2 flux, effectively decoupling the permeability-hydrophobicity trade-off. Molecular dynamics simulations corroborate this mechanism, demonstrating that the COF-VF exhibits significantly reduced adsorption affinity toward H2O compared to the pristine COF-V. In 40% RH ambient air, the battery equipped with this membrane delivers a discharge capacity of 3596 mAh g–1 and sustains cycling for 2700 h (270 cycles), a 10.8-fold improvement over unprotected cells. Advanced characterizations via DRT and DEMS confirm that the membrane promotes reversible Li2O2 formation and significantly suppresses LiOH accumulation. This work provides a multiscale strategy for molecular-level selective separation in practical energy storage.

item.title: JACS: Role of (Co)substrate Coordination to Iron in Activating Its Two-Electron Reduction of Dioxygen: Mechanism of Pterin Activation in Tryptophan Hydroxylase
item.description:
Robert R. Gipson, Ting C. Lin, Dory E. DeWeese, David F. Nielsen, Günther H. J. Peters, Edward I. Solomon
Many O2-activating mononuclear nonheme iron enzymes require substrate or cofactor/cosubstrate coordination to iron to form the key peroxy-bridged intermediate necessary for catalysis with no net change in the iron redox state. The role of (co)substrate coordination, however, remained unclear. Here, we leverage a pterin-dependent enzyme, tryptophan hydroxylase, for which cosubstrate (pterin) coordination can be experimentally controlled by the absence and presence of substrate, to explicitly determine the role of pterin coordination in O2 binding and peroxo formation. EPR, absorption, circular dichroism, and magnetic circular dichroism spectroscopies on the {FeNO}7 analog of the unobservable {FeO2}8 intermediate without and with pterin coordination demonstrate that pterin coordination induces new absorption bands and enhances NO affinity by 3.6 kcal mol–1 at 277 K. These new bands are pterin-to-iron ligand-to-metal charge-transfer transitions that compensate the electron donation from iron to NO upon NO binding. Extension of our findings on {FeNO}7 to {FeO2}8 evidences that pterin coordination stabilizes O2 binding and facilitates the two-electron transfer from pterin to {FeO2}8 to reduce the transition-state barrier for peroxo formation by 12.7 kcal mol–1, corresponding to a 1010 increase in reaction rate. The electron transfer pathways established herein underscore a unified mechanism for the pterin-dependent, α-ketoglutarate-dependent, extradiol, and intradiol dioxygenase families of mononuclear nonheme iron enzymes through which (co)substrate coordination enhances O2 binding via one-electron transfer within {FeO2}8 and two-electron donation from the (co)substrate (one to bound O2 and one to iron) to generate the peroxo species with no net redox change on the iron.

item.title: JACS: Solvent/Anion Codepleted Solvation Engineering Enables Low-Coordination Electrolytes for High-Energy and Low-Temperature Sodium-Ion Pouch Cells
item.description:
Xinhong Hu, Qinhao Shi, Jinyu Wan, Meiyi Zhang, Yongfeng Zhao, Zi-Feng Ma, Yang Si, Pengyan Wang, et al.
Widespread deployment of sodium-ion batteries demands both high energy density and reliable low-temperature (LT) operation, but is constrained by a persistent trade-off between high-voltage stability (cathode/electrolyte) and LT ion-transport kinetics. Herein, we report a solvent/anion codepleted solvation engineering strategy to construct low-coordination electrolytes through competitive anion complexation mediated by a bulky electron-deficient additive, TMSB (tris(trimethylsilyl)borate). We reveal that TMSB preferentially complexes with PF6– to suppress direct anion-Na+ coordination, while its bulky steric backbone disrupts conventional ion-pair networks and restricts excessive solvent-Na+ coordination. This strategy fundamentally boosts ionic conductivity (from 2.41 to 5.34 mS cm–1) and lowers the desolvation energy barrier (from 44.82 to 33.97 kJ mol–1). Moreover, such a strategy enables a high-modulus (2.7 GPa), inorganic-rich cathode-electrolyte interphase (CEI), which can not only mitigate surface degradation, but also suppress bulk phase transitions of cathode materials. Consequently, the electrolyte demonstrates broad compatibility across diverse cathodes (NFM, NVP, and P2-NNMO) under extreme voltage (up to 4.5 V) and temperature (−40 to 25 °C) conditions. Remarkably, the scaled-up 6.8 Ah pouch cell achieves a record-high energy density of 200 Wh kg–1 at 25 °C, while maintaining 162 Wh kg–1 even at −20 °C, offering a generalizable molecular paradigm for extreme-environment energy storage.

item.title: ACS Nano: Accelerating the Discovery of Synthesizable 2D Hybrid Double Perovskites through Human–LLM Collaborative Descriptor Engineering
item.description:
Rong Guo, Chang-Feng Wang, Ming-Gang Ju, Yilei Wu, Peiguo Liu, Qionghua Zhou, Shuaihua Lu, Zhilong Song, et al.
Two-dimensional hybrid perovskites offer exceptional structural diversity and multifunctional properties, yet their synthesis remains a major bottleneck due to low hit rates and strong reliance on empirical intuition. Here we introduce AL-SynAgent, a human-in-the-loop, ML-guided screening workflow that integrates literature-derived synthetic priors, expert-refined chemical descriptors, and active learning to assess the synthesis feasibility of two dimensional (2D) hybrid organic–inorganic rare-earth double perovskites (HORDPs). By converting LLM-assisted literature knowledge and expert chemical reasoning into system-specific computable descriptors, AL-SynAgent reduces dependence on large experimental data sets while retaining chemically interpretable decision rules. With experimental feedback from only 4.8% of candidate space, the model converged and achieved successful target-phase formation for 11 of the 14 candidates in the prospectively selected experimental set, corresponding to a hit rate of 78.6%. Screening of an enumerated virtual library of 280,000 candidates further prioritized 64,482 compositions with high predicted synthesis feasibility. Notably, three newly obtained compounds also exhibit both excellent ferroelectricity and photoluminescence, including (4-F-321)4RbEu(NO3)8, which displays an exceptionally high Curie temperature of 388 K and strong emission at 592 nm. This work establishes a practical, human-in-the-loop strategy for data-efficient prioritization of candidate compositions within chemically constrained 2D HORDP space under a standardized laboratory synthesis protocol.

item.title: ACS Nano: Engineered Living Materials: A Therapeutic Paradigm beyond Conventional Biomaterials
item.description:
Lan Yang, Jiawei Lu, Shiqi Huang, Ling Zhang
Development of biomaterials in the past two decades has profoundly advanced modern medicine. However, the relatively simple and insufficiently biological functions and lack of self-renewal capability limit their ability to dynamically adapt to complex physiological environments. Engineered living materials (eLMs) use living organisms as core functional units and provide a therapeutic approach for addressing these limitations. Thus, this review systematically summarizes the recent advancements in eLMs, beginning with an overview of the primary biological chassis, including bacteria, microalgae, fungi, and mammalian cells. eLMs hold the valuable capabilities of long-term self-sustainment and self-proliferation within complex biological environments, which are endowed with intelligent regulation. For instance, they can sense environmental signals and execute programmed functional outputs, including therapeutic protein secretion or targeted migration. Moreover, they achieve precise control over therapeutic actions, encompassing spatial localization at the disease site, temporal dynamics of the intervention, and quantitative regulation of outputs. Furthermore, we highlight the broad therapeutic applications of these dynamic systems in addressing complex diseases. Finally, we discuss the current translational challenges and future directions of the field, emphasizing the potential of integrating artificial intelligence with synthetic biology and nanomaterial engineering to develop next-generation programmable eLMs and expand their utility across diverse sectors.

item.title: JACS: General Synthesis of Functionalized 1,3-Diamines from Azoarenes and Enoates via Electrochemical Annulation and N–N Bond Cleavage Followed by Chemical Reduction
item.description:
Xinyu Chen, Yanping Sun, Pierre. H. Dixneuf, Huanfeng Jiang, Min Zhang
Despite the widespread utility of N-substituted 1,3-diamines across numerous fields, their selective synthesis directly from readily available feedstocks remains a long-standing challenge. In this context, we report a room-temperature electrochemical protocol for the synthesis of both symmetrical and unsymmetrical N,N′-disubstituted 1,3-diamines through electrochemical transformation of azoarenes with enoates, followed by convergent reduction of the resulting β-amino amides. This method features broad substrate scope, operational simplicity, no need for noble transition-metal catalysts, and high chemoselectivity. Mechanistic studies indicate that the reaction is initiated by the reduction of azoarenes, facilitated by HCOOH, while Zn2+ ions leached from anodic oxidation serve as a Lewis acid to promote intramolecular cyclization via ester amidation. Subsequent cathodic reduction drives N–N bond cleavage to afford the β-amino amide intermediates, thereby endowing azoarenes with dual-nitrogen synthon capability. This work provides a practical platform for the general synthesis of N,N′-difunctionalized 1,3-diamines and convenient late-stage structural editing of biomedicals.

item.title: JACS: A Crystalline LaCl3 Reinforced Amorphous Oxyhalide Electrolyte for Thermally Stable All-Solid-State Batteries
item.description:
Yueyue Wang, Yang Yang, Xingyu Wang, Simeng Zhang, Yang Xu, Xiangzhen Zhu, Junyi Yue, Jiamin Fu, et al.
All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) are a promising next-generation energy storage technology, but their development is often constrained by the thermal instability and high cost of solid-state electrolytes (SSEs). Amorphous oxyhalide electrolytes, while mechanically deformable, are particularly susceptible to thermal degradation. Here, we report a novel and cost-effective composite SSE fabricated by embedding LaCl3 nanocrystals within an amorphous Li–Al–O–Cl (LAOC) matrix. This unique architecture synergistically combines the high ionic conductivity of the amorphous phase with the enhanced thermal and mechanical robustness imparted by the crystalline phase. The resulting Li–La–Al–O–Cl electrolyte achieves a high room-temperature ionic conductivity exceeding 1 mS cm–1 and demonstrates exceptional thermal stability, remaining a solid powder at 150 °C, a temperature at which the baseline LAOC melts. This enhanced thermal and thermo-mechanical integrity, combined with excellent deformability, enables superior interfacial contact and stability with cathodes. The Li–La–Al–O–Cl-based ASSBs maintain stable operation at 80 °C, in stark contrast to the rapid failure of LAOC-based cells. This strategy of reinforcing a soft amorphous matrix with a rigid crystalline offers a new pathway for designing thermally robust, high-performance, and commercially viable SSEs.

item.title: JACS: Acetaldehyde-Mediated Direct Conversion of Air to Nitric Acid
item.description:
Zhiwei Liang, Linlin Zhang, Ping Wang, Mingzhu Li, Zhezheng Ding, Lixue Zhang, Ruixue Zhao, Xia Liu, et al.
The sustainable synthesis of nitric acid (HNO3) directly from air via N2 oxidation is a dream reaction but remains a long-standing challenge, owing to formidable thermodynamic and kinetic barriers. Here, we report a photoassisted thermocatalytic strategy in which acetaldehyde as a key medium enables efficient N2 oxidation to HNO3 under mild conditions. Acetaldehyde is oxidized to peracetic acid over 316L stainless steel, which subsequently generates radicals (CH3COOO•) under visible-light irradiation. These CH3COOO• radicals are highly reactive and can oxidize N2 at 200 °C and near-ambient pressures (1–5 bar), affording an HNO3 formation rate of 110.8 μmol h–1 with a concentration of 13,961 ppm and an N2 conversion of 0.45% within 2 h─approximately 2 to 4 orders of magnitude higher than previously reported systems. Notably, the kinetic irrelevance of H2O enables operation in a gas-phase flow configuration, allowing continuous and stable HNO3 production and gram-scale accumulation at the laboratory scale. This work introduces a groundbreaking reaction paradigm that couples organic radical chemistry and surface catalysis, offering a scalable and energy-efficient pathway for the green synthesis of HNO3.

item.title: JACS: Interfacial Confinement Enables Conformal IrOx Nanofilms for Low-Ir-Loading PEM Water Electrolysis
item.description:
Jun-Jie Peng, Ru-Yang Shao, Xian Zhang, Dian-Ding Sun, Zi-Ang Sun, Lan Li, Dong-Sheng Li, Yu-Qian Yan, et al.
Terawatt-scale deployment of proton-exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) requires low iridium (Ir) loading, which disrupts the catalyst layer’s in-plane electronic percolation network and severely degrades performance. Here, we overcome this bottleneck via an interfacial confinement strategy that electrostatically enriches cationic Ir intermediates on the negatively charged, oxygen-deficient TiOx surface, thereby redirecting Ir deposition from three-dimensional island growth to a two-dimensional conformal film on TiO2 supports. The resulting IrOx-NF@TiO2 catalyst with low Ir packing density maintains long-range in-plane electron percolation, reducing reliance on the high Ir loading typically required by conventional IrOx nanoparticle catalysts to establish quasi-continuous conductive pathways. At a loading of 0.166 mgIr cm−2, blade-coated membrane electrode assemblies incorporating this architecture feature ∼7 μm-thick catalyst layers with an Ir packing density of only ∼0.25 gIr cm–3, allowing an ∼84% reduction in Ir use while achieving performance comparable to that of commercial IrO2. This work highlights the potential of supported conformal IrOx catalysts as competitive candidates for next-generation low-Ir PEMWEs.

item.title: ACS Nano: Micro-LED-Activated Formaldehyde Sensing via Au Loading-Regulated Interfacial Engineering in Anatase TiO2 Nanofibers
item.description:
Euichul Shin, Kichul Lee, Yunsung Lim, Minhyun Kim, Donghyuk Kwak, Jehee Yu, Hee Jung Park, Ji-Soo Jang, et al.
Photoactivated metal-oxide gas sensors reduce the energy demand associated with continuous heating, yet selective detection of volatile organic compounds remains constrained by weak electrical transduction and complex surface oxidation pathways. Here, Au-functionalized anatase TiO2 nanofibers (Au/aTiO2 NFs) were integrated with a 395 nm microlight-emitting diode (LED) for low-power formaldehyde (HCHO) sensing. One-pot electrospinning followed by calcination enabled systematic control of Au loading while preserving the anatase nanofiber architecture. Au loading regulated TiO2 crystallite growth, defect states, dispersion, interfacial Au chemical states, and photoexcited carrier relaxation. At 0.15 wt % Au, finely dispersed Au nanoparticles produced a distinct Au/TiO2 interfacial environment and carrier-relaxation behavior, whereas higher loadings induced nanoparticle aggregation and additional nonradiative energy-loss pathways. Under UV micro-LED illumination at 2.63 mW, the optimized sensor exhibited a response of 1093 toward 1 ppm of HCHO, an estimated detection limit of 4.9 ppb, and stable operation over 40 consecutive cycles. Density functional theory calculations further supported the loading-dependent selectivity, showing that changes in the local Au environment selectively modify HCHO adsorption and bond reconstruction. These results identify local Au-site density as a key design parameter governing interfacial reactivity and molecular selectivity in low-power photoactivated gas sensing.

item.title: JACS: Empowering HFIP as a Radical Trifluoromethylating Reagent by Photoelectrochemical Iron Catalysis
item.description:
Naifu Zhou, Xinyi Wang, Huaiyu Hu, Tong Mu, Xiao-Song Xue, Lu Song, Niankai Fu
The development of practical synthetic methods for incorporating trifluoromethyl (CF3) groups into organic scaffolds is of paramount importance in medicinal chemistry, as such modifications profoundly modulate the physicochemical properties of drug candidates. 1,1,1,3,3,3-Hexafluoro-2-propanol (HFIP) is widely utilized as a unique solvent in synthetic chemistry and also represents a promising CF3 source due to its high availability and low cost. Here we report an unprecedented photoelectrochemical iron-catalyzed protocol for radical trifluoromethylation that employs commercially accessible HFIP as the CF3 radical precursor. This method enables efficient trifluoromethylation of unactivated arenes, heteroarenes, and alkenes with a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. Notably, this photoelectrocatalytic system is readily scalable for practical synthetic applications, and its utility has been demonstrated in the trifluoromethylation of peptides, allowing preferential modification of tryptophan residues in a chemoselective fashion.

item.title: ACS Nano: Electrically Reconfigurable Silicon Carbide Nanophotonic Cavities on Thin-Film Lithium Niobate
item.description:
San Lam Ng, Georgii Grechko, Vladislav Bushmakin, Rainer Stöhr, Vadim Vorobyov, Roman Kolesov, Jörg Wrachtrup
Interfacing integrated photonics with solid-state spin defects holds great promise for future quantum networks, but the scaling of spin-photon architectures is hindered by frequency mismatches arising from fabrication-induced variations in photonic cavity resonances and inhomogeneous optical transition frequencies of individual spins. These challenges call for a photonic platform with deterministic and wide-range tunability. Here, we demonstrate a hybrid nanophotonic platform based on direct bonding of silicon carbide photonic crystal nanocavity arrays onto a thin-film lithium niobate-on-insulator, enabling deterministic electrical tuning of multiple SiC nanocavities into mutual spectral resonance. By exploiting the strong electro-optic response of lithium niobate, we achieve continuous and wide-range cavity tuning of 380 GHz (∼1.1 nm), sufficient to compensate both cavity disorder and spin spectral inhomogeneity. The nanocavities balance strong optical confinement with electrical tunability, exhibiting a theoretical Purcell factor of approximately 400. This hybrid platform enables electrically reconfigurable spin-photon interfaces for large-scale integrated quantum photonics.

item.title: ACS Nano: Fluorinated Copper(I) Iodine Cluster Scintillators Enable High-Temperature X-ray Imaging
item.description:
Cao Fang, Dong Tan, Yujing Gao, Zhipeng Zhang, Xi Kang, Shuo Yu, Shoubo Wei, Zhijia Hu, et al.
The development of scintillators that maintain excellent performance under high temperatures is a critical challenge. Here, by simply replacing the triphenylphosphine ligand with its fluorinated analogue, we successfully switched the emission pathway of Cu2I2 clusters from pure phosphorescence to a hybrid phosphorescence/thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) mechanism, enabling adaptive high-temperature X-ray imaging. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that the fluorination strategy reduces the singlet–triplet energy gap to an exceptionally small value of 35 meV, thereby promoting efficient reverse intersystem crossing. The TADF contribution reaches 95.7% at room temperature. This temperature-responsive characteristic endows the fluorinated cluster with adaptive X-ray imaging capability across a broad temperature window from 293 to 413 K, overcoming the thermal quenching phenomenon in traditional phosphorescence-only scintillators. This work establishes a molecular design approach for smart scintillators capable of reliable operation in demanding thermal environments.

item.title: JACS: Ammonia-Driven Nanoscale Surface Restructuring of Copper Catalysts during Nitrate Reduction Reaction
item.description:
Yujie Peng, Mael Brule, Yawei Zhou, Beatriz Roldan Cuenya, Christopher S. Kley
The electrolyte and applied potential are known to impact a catalyst’s structure and performance, yet the role of reaction intermediates and products in driving surface evolution remains largely unexplored. Here, using electrochemical atomic force microscopy, we show that the dynamic restructuring of copper (Cu) surfaces during nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) directly correlates with the rate and selectivity of ammonia (NH3) formation. At moderate overpotentials, where nitrite formation dominates, lateral expansion of Cu terraces is observed, whereas rapid NH3 formation at higher cathodic potentials induces Cu adislands enriched in low-coordinated step sites, revealing distinct restructuring pathways that accompany the transition from nitrite- to ammonia-selective NO3RR. These transformations are rationalized by an NH3-mediated Cu dissolution-redeposition mechanism. Our results identify reaction products as active modulators of catalyst surface structure, establishing a framework for understanding reaction-driven catalyst restructuring and enabling in situ control of catalyst surfaces through the interfacial reaction environment.

item.title: JACS: Hybrid Weakly Coordinated Solvents for Fast-Charging and Wide-Temperature Sodium-Ion Full Batteries
item.description:
Yun Wan, Xiaoyan Shi, Yuerong Li, Zhiming Zhou, Xu Xu, Xinhui Zeng, Xiaosa Zhang, Xunzhu Zhou, et al.
The application of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) in wide-temperature and fast-charging scenarios is severely constrained by the performance limitations of electrolytes. Conventional ester-based electrolytes struggle to simultaneously achieve high ionic conductivity, low desolvation energy, and excellent interfacial stability. Herein, we propose a hybrid solvent system comprising ethyl propionate and ethoxy(pentafluoro)cyclotriphosphazene (PFPN), aiming to synergistically enhance the rate capability and temperature adaptability of SIBs. The relatively weak coordination ability of both solvents effectively promotes anion participation in solvation structure, significantly lowering the Na+ desolvation energy barrier and inducing the formation of stable, inorganic-rich electrode/electrolyte interphases. Meanwhile, the dual-solvent combination increases the diversity of solvation configurations and reduces ion clustering, thereby enhancing ionic conductivity. The intrinsic nonflammability and excellent film-forming ability of PFPN further enhance safety and synergistically strengthen interfacial stability. Therefore, Prussian blue||hard carbon full cells operate stably over a wide temperature range from −50 to 100 °C. Notably, ampere-hour-level pouch cells deliver a capacity retention of 86.3% after 300 cycles at 25 °C and maintain stable operation for over 100 cycles even at −20 and 80 °C. This solvent synergy strategy offers a practical new pathway for the development of electrolytes for SIBs in extreme environments.

item.title: Nano Letters: Endogenous Fe Single-Atom-Induced Short-Range Graphitization Enables Integrated Electromagnetic Wave Absorption and Thermal Management in PTFE Composites
item.description:
Xiao Liu, Yongxin Qian, Daguang Li, Xuefei Xu, Gengping Wan, Lei Yu, Guizhen Wang
Modern electronics require polymer composites that integrate electromagnetic wave absorption (EWA) and thermal dissipation, yet these functions impose competing structural requirements. Herein, we construct Fe single-atom@short-range graphitized porous carbon (Fe1@SGC) that integrates electromagnetic attenuation and thermal conduction within a single material. Distinct from conventional exogenous metal-introduction routes, egg white serves as both the carbon source and coordination medium, enabling Fe single-atom anchoring without metal salts or organic ligands. Fe single atoms induce charge redistribution, polarization centers, and local ordering of carbon domains, synergistically regulating dielectric loss, thermal transport, and impedance matching. The multiscale carbon network further promotes electromagnetic wave penetration and multiple reflections/scattering. After incorporation into polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), the Fe1@SGC/PTFE composite achieves a maximum effective absorption bandwidth of 7.92 GHz and improved thermal conductivity. This work establishes endogenous single-atom-induced local graphitization as a ligand-free and structurally precise strategy for designing single-component fillers toward integrated EWA and thermal management.

item.title: JACS: Linker Steric Hindrance-Induced Defect Engineering Enables Oxygen Vacancy-Rich MOFs for Pollutant Degradation
item.description:
Weiyu Ye, Yizhang Li, Xiaoxue Kou, Linjing Tong, Yong Shen, Rui Gao, Siming Huang, Fang Zhu, et al.
The widespread contamination of water by emerging contaminants (ECs) demands the development of efficient remediation technologies. Although advanced oxidation processes reliant on reactive oxygen species (ROS) show promise, they typically depend on energy- or reagent-intensive activation methods. Here, we introduce a linker steric hindrance-induced defect engineering (LSH-DE) strategy for metal–organic frameworks, which enables catalytic ROS generation using molecular oxygen (O2) as a benign terminal oxidant at ambient temperature and pressure. By systematically modulating the steric bulk of organic linkers, we precisely create missing-linker defects and direct the formation of oxygen vacancy (Vo) in robust Ce-UiO-66 during a rapid 15 min synthesis. Spectroscopic and computational analyses confirm that these oxygen vacancies promote O2 adsorption and activation to yield superoxide radicals (•O2–). The optimized catalyst, Ce-UiO-66-(CH3)2, demonstrates superior activity in degrading ubiquitous ECs without requiring external energy inputs or chemical mediators. Furthermore, integration of Ce-UiO-66-(CH3)2 into a membrane-based recirculating flow-through system enabled sustained water treatment, maintaining >90% BPA removal over 48 h with a high water permeance of 101.5 L m–2 h–1 bar–1. This work presents a general and sustainable approach for designing catalytic defects in MOFs, advancing the development of green, next-generation water purification technologies.

item.title: ACS Nano: Frozen 2D Adatom Gas at the Surface of Gold–Copper Alloys
item.description:
Han Xuan Wong, Yuyi Yan, Kang’an Wang, Fujia Liu, Kate Reidy, Man Guo, Ethan J. Crumlin, Andrew M. Minor, et al.
Isolated, undercoordinated metal atoms exhibit enhanced reactivity central to catalysis, yet their stabilization on surfaces remains challenging. In heterogeneous single-atom catalysis, activity derives from interactions between individual atoms and a host matrix, but the absence of stabilizing ligands often leads to diffusion, aggregation, and sintering, obscuring structure–activity relationships. On metal surfaces, reactivity is typically limited to sparse, dynamic, undercoordinated sites lining step edges or lattice defects. Here we report a defect-engineering strategy to stabilize isolated adatoms on dilute metal alloy substrates. Scanning tunneling microscopy reveals a high density of uniformly distributed adatoms on Au–Cu(111) terraces that persist under thermal cycling. Combined experiments and modeling attribute this stability to alloy-induced subsurface dislocation networks that trap adatoms and suppress diffusion, forming a two-dimensional frozen gas. These adatoms act as a reactive reservoir, enabling on-surface coordination chemistry inaccessible on pure metals, and providing insights into atomic-scale processes on the surfaces of defect-engineered alloys with implications for heterogeneous catalysis.

item.title: Nano Letters: Sequential Monomer Addition Regulates Hydration in Branched Poly(aryl piperidinium) Membranes for Water Electrolysis
item.description:
Zhenyang Zhou, Deyu Zhu, Lebin Cai, Quyu Yang, Liang Dong, Fuqing Yu, Wei Guo, Qiang Zhao, et al.
The conductivity-swelling trade-off limits anion exchange membranes (AEMs) for water electrolysis. Here, we investigated how the timing of tetraphenylmethane (TPM) incorporation influences precursor assembly and membrane hydration in poly(aryl piperidinium) AEMs. Introducing TPM before backbone extension alters precursor formation and favors a more uniform distribution of hydrophilic domains in the resulting membranes. Spectroscopic and NMR analyses further associate this route with enhanced hydrogen-bond organization and increased local mobility within the hydrated membranes. The optimized P-TPM5 membrane reaches an OH– conductivity of 229.4 ± 6 mS cm–1 at 80 °C while maintaining a swelling ratio of approximately 15%. In an AEM water electrolyzer containing a NiFe-LDH anode and Pt/C cathode, the membrane delivers 5.74 A cm–2 at 2.0 V and operates for more than 1100 h in a staged-current test. These results identify the timing of branching-unit incorporation as a synthesis variable for tailoring hydration environments and improving the conductivity-swelling balance of AEMs.

item.title: JACS: Molecular Mechanophores Based on Stress-Enhanced Exciton Transition between Phosphorescent Probes and Polymer Matrix
item.description:
Jinzheng Chen, Yuhong Zhou, Yiling Miao, Guanbo Wang, Haiyan Zheng, Yi Zhang, Zhenguo Chi, Yongming Chen, et al.
Mechanophores provide an in situ and remote tool for quantifying invisible stress in polymers by photonic signals, offering distinct advantages for stress distribution analysis of large-area surfaces and instrument-free stress observation. However, achieving an ideal mechanophore that integrates with sensitive, reversible, and molecular-level stress sensing is attractive yet challenging. Here, we report practical guidance for developing ideal mechanophores that promote the molecular probe’s exciton transition for room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) under stress, through the “assisted lowest triplet (T1) state” of the adjacent polymer chain. Systematic analyses of numerous organic probes reveal that a small energy gap (ΔEM < 0.4 eV) between the probe’s lowest singlet (S1) and the polymer’s T1 states is an empirical guideline for stress-enhanced RTP. The probe-doped polymer system demonstrates not only a remarkable increase in RTP intensity of over 2000-fold upon 160 MPa but also a low stress threshold of ∼2 MPa, which is robust under 0–10 MPa cyclic pressure loading/unloading over 500 cycles. Such RTP mechanophores enable noninvasive, reversible, and molecular-level stress detection in polymers. Their doped polymers have shown potential applications in various fields for real-time sensing of stress and its uneven distribution through visual afterglow.

item.title: ACS Nano: Hybridization State Engineering of Coal Pitch-Based Carbon Materials Enabling Ultrastable Aqueous Zinc–Iodine Batteries with 150,000 Cycles
item.description:
Xixian Li, Yanting Duan, Qi Yang, Zui Tao, Jiankun Wang, Na Jiang, Ziqiang Liu, Mingyu Li, et al.
Carbon materials with superior porosity and conductivity are widely adopted in aqueous zinc–iodine batteries to host iodine, but suffer from the polyiodide shuttle and cycling stability challenges. Traditional strategies mainly focus on pore structure engineering or heteroatom doping of carbon hosts to confine iodine, but fail to address the sluggish iodine conversion kinetics. Herein, we initially reveal the significant yet overlooked role of hybridization state in reforming the carbon intrinsic activity toward high-efficiency iodine conversion chemistry. With pitch-derived porous carbon as an example, we controllably regulate the C(sp2)/C(sp3) ratio (from 1.23 to 2.21) while maintaining high surface area. These properties lower the activation energy of iodine conversion and effectively suppress the polyiodide shuttle. The zinc–iodine battery exhibits ultrahigh cycling stability after 150,000 cycles and a low self-discharging rate with only 12.5% capacity loss after 20 days. Ah-level pouch cell with 66.6 mgiodine cm–2 achieves a cumulative discharging capacity of 103.51 Ah. The hybridization engineering was successfully extended to commercial porous carbon (YP-50F), prolonging the lifespan from 7425 to 27,000 cycles. This work presents a hybridization state engineering strategy to reform the intrinsic activity of the carbon host to favor the iodine conversion chemistry and beyond.

item.title: ACS Nano: 5DSTEM of Liquid-Phase Nanocrystal Growth Bridges Ensemble Kinetics and Nanoscale Dynamics
item.description:
Serin Lee, Colin Ophus, Jennifer A. Dionne
Resolving how ensemble growth kinetics emerge from particle- and grain-level dynamics is essential for predictive control of nanocrystal synthesis. Here, time-resolved four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4DSTEM), extended into five dimensions (5DSTEM) through continuous acquisition, is used to simultaneously resolve morphology, crystallographic orientation, and lattice strain during Au nanocrystal growth in aqueous HAuCl4. Although ensemble growth follows surface-reaction-limited kinetics, individual nanoparticles exhibit distinct pathways, including continuous growth and discrete coalescence through oriented attachment. These pathways display characteristic orientation dynamics, with stable or gradually selected orientations during continuous growth and abrupt reconfiguration followed by alignment during coalescence. At the ensemble level, the out-of-plane orientation distribution is established early and remains stable, whereas in-plane orientations remain broadly distributed without global alignment. Tensile strain develops progressively from particle surfaces and interfaces, directly linking lattice distortion with evolving morphology and crystallographic structure. By connecting ensemble kinetics with particle- and grain-resolved structural evolution, 5DSTEM provides a general framework for uncovering heterogeneous growth mechanisms and for relating synthesis pathways to structure-dependent properties in functional nanomaterials.

item.title: ACS Nano: Nano-Optical Switching of Photochromic Material through Ultraviolet and Visible Plasmon Nanofocusing
item.description:
Takayuki Umakoshi, Hiroshi Arata, Prabhat Verma
Optical control of photochromic properties is essential for optoelectronic devices. The manipulation of such properties has been limited to the microscale because of the wave nature of light; however, scaling down the volume is highly demanded for the future nanosized devices. Herein, we demonstrate optical switching at the nanoscale in an organic photochromic material. Photochromic materials such as diarylethene derivatives exhibit two different states with distinct optical and electronic properties under ultraviolet (UV) and visible light irradiation. We employed plasmon nanofocusing for optical switching of photochromic materials, which allowed the creation of a nanolight source at the apex of a tapered aluminum structure over a broad frequency range. We achieved in situ wavelength control between visible and UV light at the nanoscale for photochromic reactions. Using this technique, we demonstrated nanoscale optical switching between the two states of diarylethene. The switching performance was confirmed for at least nine cycles without degradation. This demonstration would constitute a significant step toward next-generation optoelectronic devices and benefit diverse scientific fields owing to the broad wavelength tunability of plasmon nanofocusing.

item.title: JACS: Functional Specialization of Coordination Spheres Enables Site-Selective Aromatic C–H Isotope Exchange in Ni Single-Atom Catalysts
item.description:
Jie Chen, Wengang Liu, Auttaphon Chachvalvutikul, Mohammad M. Jaffar, Wenze Liu, Pengyu Du, Longyue Hu, Xinshui Lei, et al.
Engineering single-atom catalysts has predominantly focused on tailoring the primary coordination sphere, whereas whether distinct coordination spheres can be endowed with independent catalytic functions remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate the functional specialization of coordination spheres by constructing a phosphorus-modified Ni–N2O2 single-atom catalyst for site-selective C–H deuteration. Advanced spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations show that phosphorus is incorporated outside the preserved primary Ni–N2O2 coordination environment and support an O-linked phosphorus environment as a preferential second-sphere motif. This architecture decouples substrate recognition from catalytic activation. Specifically, second-sphere phosphorus selectively recognizes and anchors the amino group of haloanilines to dictate deuteration site selectivity, whereas the preserved primary Ni–N2O2 coordination sphere promotes H2 activation and undergoes H2-assisted regeneration following D2O-induced hydroxylation, facilitated by P–O–Ni electronic communication, thereby sustaining efficient catalytic turnover. Consequently, the catalyst achieves highly site-selective C–H deuteration of chloro-, bromo-, and iodoanilines using H2 and D2O while completely preserving carbon–halogen bonds, whereas the phosphorus-free analogue exhibits negligible activity. This work identifies the structural origin and catalytic function of second-sphere phosphorus and establishes functional specialization of coordination spheres as a general design principle for independently programming substrate recognition and catalytic turnover in single-atom catalysis.

item.title: JACS: Simultaneous Selective Recognition of Two Different Anions within a Hydrogen/Halogen-Bonding Cage
item.description:
Bailee R. Smith, Rosemary J. Goodwin, Nicholas G. White
The search for selective anion receptors that can function in water is a longstanding challenge in supramolecular chemistry, motivated by anions’ fundamental roles (and potential applications) in biological, environmental, and industrial processes. Here, we incorporate halogen and hydrogen bond donors into an easy-to-prepare organic cage molecule and demonstrate that this can bind anions at either or both of a halogen-bonding pocket and hydrogen-bonding pockets depending on the nature of the anions and the solvent. The halogen-bonding pocket comprising six bromopyridinium donors is a potent host for iodide anions and can selectively bind this guest in water as strongly as biological iodide binders (Ka = 43,000 M–1 measured by 1H NMR spectroscopy) with the exclusion of other halide anions. In DMSO/water mixtures, the hydrogen-bonding pockets are able to recognize chloride anions, resulting in the formation of mixed anion iodide/chloride complexes with an iodide bound in the center of the cage and chlorides in the peripheral binding sites. This demonstrates the exquisite selectivity afforded by halogen-bonding systems and reveals a general route to a range of supramolecular anion hosts that bind multiple guests in different locations.

item.title: JACS: Anti -Dihydroxylation-Enabled Dual-Resolution Profiling and Imaging of Fatty Acid C═C Bond Isomers
item.description:
Zhijun Zhu, Shuling Xu, William J. Heelan, Penghsuan Huang, Hua Zhang, Gaoyuan Lu, Amy B. Banta, Jason M. Peters, et al.
Lipids are essential for membrane structure, signaling, and stress adaptation. Their diverse biological roles are largely dictated by the presence of C═C bonds in unsaturated fatty acids (FAs), which vary in both position and geometry. However, unambiguous characterization and in situ mapping of these two structural features have remained longstanding analytical challenges. Here, we present a stereochemistry-preserved chemical derivatization strategy coupled with trapped ion mobility spectrometry-tandem MS (TIMS-MS/MS), enabling complete resolution of both FA C═C bond position and geometry within a single workflow. This approach facilitates rapid and quantitative profiling of dynamic cis–trans isomerization in bacteria under diverse stress conditions and, notably, reveals a previously unrecognized dose-dependent antibiotic adaptation mechanism in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a multidrug-resistant pathogen. To translate this strategy to spatially resolved analyses, we developed an in situ derivatization workflow for mass spectrometry imaging, which uncovers the spatial heterogeneity of FA isomers in proximally cocultured, clinically relevant polymicrobial pathogens. These findings highlight colony-specific spatial dynamics of cis and trans lipid isomers and suggest lipid-mediated metabolic interactions between co-occurring microbial species. Together, this integrated platform enables both quantitative and spatial interrogation of lipid isomerization, providing new opportunities to systematically investigate its roles in microbial physiology, pathogenesis, and beyond.

item.title: ACS Nano: Silencing MSR1 in Macrophages Attenuates the Cochlear Foreign Body Response and Preserves Electrode–Neural Interface
item.description:
Anning Chen, Yunyou You, Jie Yang, Ying Zhang, Jing Pan, Yongdong Lin, Andrej Kral, Jie Tang, et al.
Cochlear implantation (CI) provides effective auditory rehabilitation for patients with severe-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss. Implantation can nevertheless induce local foreign body response (FBR) and cochlear fibrosis, motivating strategies to reduce tissue reactions and preserve cochlear integrity. Macrophages play a key role in FBR, but their functions are multiple and stage-dependent, and indiscriminate intervention may aggravate cochlear injury. Therefore, more precise strategies are needed to modulate macrophage-mediated FBR after CI. Here, through transcriptomic profiling of cochlear tissues from rats 30 days after cochlear implantation, we identified macrophage scavenger receptor 1 (MSR1) as a prominent signature after CI. In vitro assays further verified the role of MSR1 in reshaping macrophage phenotype and inflammatory activation. To achieve targeted MSR1 regulation in the cochlea, we engineered iRGD-modified extracellular vesicles to deliver siMSR1 (iRGD-EV/siMSR1). iRGD modification enhanced macrophage uptake of EV and enabled efficient siRNA delivery. In a rat CI model, local administration of iRGD-EV/siMSR1 reduced cochlear fibrotic tissue formation and decreased fibrosis-related protein expression. Moreover, iRGD-EV/siMSR1 preserved spiral ganglion neurons and myelin structures, contributing to residual hearing protection after implantation. Early stage analysis at 7 days after implantation showed that iRGD-EV/siMSR1 suppressed macrophage inflammatory activation, reduced TGF-β1-related profibrotic signaling, regulated matrix remodeling, and limited early apoptosis. These findings identify MSR1 as a promising molecular target for cochlear implant-induced FBR and support iRGD-EV/siMSR1 as a potentially translatable strategy for attenuating cochlear fibrosis and preserving the cochlear neural interface, also highlighting the importance of considering neural health when modulating macrophage-mediated responses to cochlear implants.

item.title: ACS Nano: Chronic Stress-Triggerable Nanoprodrugs Ameliorate Metabolic Abnormalities Driven by Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal Axis Dysregulation in Early Alzheimer’s Disease
item.description:
Xiaomeng Yu, Fan Yang, Yining Liu, Jiyao Xie, Jiamei Xie, Yihan Chen, Jin Chang, Yan Dou
Chronic stress-induced dysregulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis is a crucial early risk factor that triggers brain energy metabolism disorders to accelerate the onset and progression of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Herein, an amphiphilic precursor conjugate of ginsenoside Rc (Rc) covalently linked with a reactive oxygen species-sensitive thioketo bond is constructed to form stimuli-responsive prodrug assemblies, which are further modified with the TGN-Tet1 dual-ligand fusion peptide TPL to obtain a chronic stress-triggerable programmed nanoprodrug (TLRN). Following TPL-mediated blood-brain barrier penetration and neuronal preferential targeting, nanoprodrugs specifically disintegrate to selectively release active Rc in the chronic stress-induced excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) microenvironment. Benefiting from the restoration of HPA axis homeostasis by normalizing glucocorticoid receptor nuclear translocation, TLRN treatment exhibits multifaceted rectification of cerebral metabolic abnormalities, including enhancing glucose uptake, promoting oxidative phosphorylation, and mitigating mitochondrial dysfunction. In young amyloid precursor protein/presenilin 1 (APP/PS1) transgenic mouse models exposed to chronic stress, this intervention can alleviate brain energy deprivation and amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation, ultimately rescuing depressive-like behaviors and cognitive deficits, offering a promising approach for early prevention and flexible management of AD at high risk of chronic stress.

item.title: ACS Nano: Ultrasound-Responsive Electroactive Polyetheretherketone Scaffold Promotes Bioenergetic Bone Regeneration by Regulating Mitochondrial Permeability Transition Pores
item.description:
Meihua Zhang, Lingzhu Yu, Yangrui Chen, Mengmeng Ming, Bin Luo, Yao Wu
Mitochondrial dysfunction and energy metabolic imbalance in senescent bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) are critical pathological foundations for senile bone regeneration. Existing therapeutic strategies suffer from a lack of active mitochondrial bioenergetic driving forces, failing to effectively reverse energy metabolic suppression of senescent BMSCs. Here, an ultrasound-activated electroactive scaffold was constructed by anchoring barium titanate-transition metal carbide (MXene@BaTiO3) heterojunctions on the surface of polyetheretherketone (PEEK) to reactivate mitochondrial energy metabolism and promote bone regeneration under senescence-associated bone loss conditions. These heterojunctions adhere to BMSC membranes and generate electrical stimulation upon ultrasound stimulation, which significantly inhibits abnormal opening of mitochondrial permeability transition pores (mPTP), reduces leakage of mtDNA and Cyt c, and maintains membrane potential stability. Mechanistic investigations reveal that electrical stimulation activates the PI3K/Akt/MDM2 signaling axis to promote the degradation of accumulated p53, which relieves the competitive binding of p53 to TRAP1, thereby restoring TRAP1-CypD-mediated mPTP gating and mitochondrial homeostasis. Consequently, this ultrasound-activated electroactive scaffold drives mitochondrial energy metabolism and osteogenic differentiation of senescence-like BMSCs in vitro, which is further confirmed in a rat model. These results demonstrate the potential of this electroactive scaffold as a regulator of mitochondrial energy metabolism for senescence-associated bone regeneration.

item.title: JACS: Photomediated Chromium-Catalyzed Regio-, Diastereo-, and Enantioselective Deoxygenative Coupling of Activated Allylic and Propargylic Alcohols with Aldehydes
item.description:
Zhong-Xian Li, Jia-Cheng Wu, Jun-Jie Yang, Ying Li, Sheng-Ye Zhang, Jun Zhu
Chromium-catalyzed asymmetric Nozaki–Hiyama–Kishi (NHK) reaction is a powerful tool for constructing synthetically valuable enantioenriched homoallylic alcohols and allenols. However, catalytic asymmetric NHK-type coupling of allylic or propargylic C–O electrophiles remains largely underdeveloped. Herein, we report a photomediated chromium-catalyzed deoxygenative coupling of activated allylic and propargylic alcohols with aldehydes, enabling the synthesis of a variety of chiral homoallylic alcohols with wide structural diversity and allenols. The reactions were performed under mild conditions, and a wide range of synthetically useful functional groups was found to be well tolerated. Importantly, this method provides a straightforward way for the construction of homoallylic alcohols bearing a chiral quaternary carbon center with high ee and dr. Furthermore, stereodivergent access to all four homoallylic alcohol stereoisomers is realized through orthogonal combinations of Z/E-configured allylic alcohols and R/S-configured ligands. Combined experimental and computational mechanistic studies provided insight into the key catalytic intermediate and the origin of stereocontrol.

item.title: ACS Nano: Shield-and-Amplify Nanoparticle Vaccines Retune Immunodominance for Broad Protection against SARS-CoV-2
item.description:
Wenhui Xue, Hong Wang, Sibo Zhang, Hai Li, Lingyan Cui, Miaolin Lan, Yarong Zeng, Hongjing Liu, et al.
Antigenic variation severely constrains the durability and breadth of vaccine-induced protection against rapidly evolving viruses. Although conserved epitopes can support cross-variant immunity, antibody responses to viral glycoproteins are often biased toward exposed, mutable immunodominant epitopes, leaving conserved protective sites subdominant. We previously identified a cryptic, conserved class 5 epitope (the 6D6/7D6 epitope) on the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain (RBD) capable of eliciting broad cross-neutralization. Here, we present a modular “shield-and-amplify” nanoparticle vaccination strategy to redirect immunodominance toward this subdominant epitope. We engineered site-specific N-linked glycans─alongside the native N343 glycan to mask variable immunodominant regions while preserving accessibility to the class 5 epitope. The resulting glycan-masked RBD antigen (RGM) was displayed on p239 nanoparticles via nanobody-mediated assembly, yielding multivalent RGM@p239 immunogens. Antigenic profiling revealed that glycan shielding preserved recognition by 6D6 and 7D6 antibodies while reducing binding of representative class 1–4 antibodies by at least 80%. In immunized animals, RGM@p239 enriched 7D6-competitive serum antibodies blocking approximately 70–80% of serum binding to RGM and broadened cross-variant neutralization against 8 representative variant strains, including detectable activity against Omicron lineages. Furthermore, RGM@p239 reduced disease severity after Omicron EG.1 challenge in a hamster model. These results support a model in which glycan shielding and nanoparticle multivalency act as complementary immune-focusing modules: shielding attenuates competing responses, while multivalency amplifies responses to conserved subdominant epitopes. This study establishes a nanovaccine design strategy to address antigenic variation by focusing immunity on conserved viral vulnerabilities.

item.title: ACS Nano: Switching of Exciton-Polaritons in Covalent Organic Framework-Based Optical Resonators through Interaction with the Molecular Environment
item.description:
Beatriz de Sola-Báez, Tigmansu Pal, Diego M. Juela, Laura Caliò, Mauricio E. Calvo, Juan F. Galisteo-López, Jesús Hernández-Saz, Miriam Herrera, et al.
We report a demonstration of a covalent organic framework (COF) integrated into an optical cavity for the realization of exciton–polaritons and their reversible switching through changes in the surrounding molecular environment. Films of COF nanoplates were integrated into Fabry–Pérot resonators engineered to achieve spectral matching between cavity modes and COF excitonic transitions, yielding strong light–matter coupling with a Rabi splitting above 300 meV. The cavity architecture preserves accessibility of the porous framework, enabling interaction with guest molecules. The potential of this interplay is shown by exposing the resonators to water vapor, which induces both a redshift and a pronounced reduction of the COF optical absorption. The observed hypochromic effect drives a reversible shift from strong to weak coupling, effectively switching exciton–polaritons on and off, as guest molecules are desorbed from or adsorbed in the reticular material host. The process is reversible upon desorption, with preservation of structural and optical integrity. These results establish COFs as a versatile platform for chemically tunable polaritonic systems, opening avenues for responsive photonic devices, sensing, and control of light–matter interactions in nanostructured materials.

item.title: JACS: Magnetic Resonance Silent Activatable Probe with Massive Signal Amplification for Rapid Detection of Inflammation-Associated Fibrogenesis
item.description:
Yuanlin Zhang, Ilknur Ay, Fumitaro Masaki, Veronica Clavijo Jordan, Hua Ma, Iris Y. Zhou, Chloe Brasket, Dongjun Li, et al.
Biomarker-specific molecular imaging is vital in precision medicine. However, a fundamental challenge of most molecular imaging methods is the difficulty of distinguishing specific molecular signal from nonspecific signal arising from the distribution of the molecular probe. This is even more pronounced in metabolically active organs such as the kidney and liver where the probe may concentrate prior to elimination. As a result, almost all molecular imaging relies on delayed imaging to achieve specificity, but this constrains clinical throughput and impedes rapid assessment of the diseased organ. Here, we report a magnetic resonance (MR) probe, Fe(II)-IAFP2, which combines 3 drivers of relaxivity enhancement to decouple disease specificity from probe distribution. Fe(II)-IAFP2 is MR-silent in its Fe(II) state, producing negligible MR signal even at high concentrations. In inflammatory, fibrogenic microenvironments common to many diseases, rapid oxidation to Fe(III) activates MR enhancement, while reversible aldehyde-mediated binding to remodeled extracellular matrix further amplifies relaxivity and promotes retention at the site of tissue injury. This dual activation–retention mechanism enables robust signal generation within minutes of administration. In mouse models of renal and liver fibrogenesis, Fe(II)-IAFP2 generated disease-associated MR contrast within minutes after intravenous administration. Together, this work demonstrates an effective strategy for rapid, activity-based molecular MR imaging through the combination of pathological activation and complementary tissue retention.

item.title: JACS: A Double-Tethered Metallacyclobutadiene Catalyst for Cyclic Polymer Synthesis
item.description:
Vishal Chakravorty, Courtney M. Sever, Sayanil Ghosh, Palak Rakesh, Cody W. Daneluik, Ion Ghiviriga, Adam S. Veige
The synthesis, characterization, and catalytic polymerization results of an unprecedented double-tethered metallacyclobutadiene complex (4) are discussed. Complex 4 is active for the polymerization of acetylenes. Complex 4 polymerizes tert-butylacetylene to form cyclic poly(tert-butylacetylene). Evidence for a cyclic polymer topology comes from size exclusion chromatography (SEC) and intrinsic viscosity (η) measurements. This unusual reactivity of complex 4 toward a tert-alkylacetylene is attributed to its fluxional behavior, which arises from the double tethering of an yne-ol proligand (2) that facilitates monomer access and catalytic turnover. The preliminary scope of this complex design is demonstrated through modification of the yne-ol proligand, which afforded two additional double-tethered metallacyclobutadiene complexes 10 and 11 that are also catalytically active for polymerization.

item.title: ACS Nano: Polarization-Controlled Dual-Mode Switching in van der Waals α-In2Se3 Memristors for Multitime-Scale Reservoir Computing
item.description:
Soo-Hyun Lee, Jong-Hyun Kim, Hyeong-Kyu Jin, Deji Akinwande, Hyun-Yong Yu
Electrochemical-metallization (ECM) memristors can implement both nonvolatile memory switching and volatile threshold switching, making them attractive for neuromorphic and reservoir computing; however, the stochastic formation of metallic filaments causes variability in the threshold voltage and switching instability. Here, we report a van der Waals α-In2Se3-based ferroelectric-semiconductor ECM (FeS-ECM) memristor in which a bidirectionally polarized α-In2Se3 layer is inserted between the inert electrode and the switching layer. The out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization, programmed through a decoupled in-plane poling terminal, deterministically selects within the low-compliance operating regime between nonvolatile bipolar memory switching and volatile unipolar threshold switching within a single device, with a coefficient of variation in the set voltage of 4.7% and stable operation over more than 9000 cycles. Exploiting these two modes, a single α-In2Se3 platform exhibits both the volatile reservoir dynamics and the nonvolatile conductance modulation required for the readout weights of a physical reservoir-computing system, in which the pulse width electrically programs multiple relaxation time constants. This pulse-width multitime scale reconfigurability enables efficient temporal information processing, demonstrated through MNIST classification and chaotic time-series prediction.

item.title: ACS Nano: Direct Observation of Chirality-Dependent Berry Curvature Dipole via Cross-Axial Nonlinear Hall Effect in Trigonal Te
item.description:
Jaehyun Lee, Junhee Shin, Daryll J. C. Dalayoan, Miju Park, Changhee Sohn, Gang Qiu, Noejung Park, Binghai Yan, et al.
Quantum geometric quantities, such as Berry curvature (BC) and quantum metric, are known to govern the physical and topological properties of materials, making access to these quantities critically important for the comprehensive understanding of the materials. Chiral crystals offer a natural platform in which structural handedness can control quantum geometry and nonlinear transport, but direct experimental access to the quantum geometric quantities has remained elusive. Here, we show that trigonal tellurium (Te) hosts an enantiomer-dependent Berry curvature dipole (BCD) that can be accessed through the measurement of the cross-axial nonlinear Hall effect (NHE), unlike in previously studied in-plane configurations, where the BCD contribution vanishes. Angle-resolved measurements on left- and right-handed Te devices reveal a second-order transverse response whose sign reverses with crystal chirality. The extracted cross-axial nonlinear susceptibility, χyxz, exceeds the in-plane susceptibility, χxxx, by more than two-fold, indicating a strong BCD-driven contribution. First-principles calculations attribute this behavior to a topologically nontrivial hedgehog-like BC texture near the H points and predict a BCD that reverses sign between opposite enantiomers, consistent with experiment. These results establish cross-axial nonlinear Hall transport as a symmetry-selective probe of chirality-controlled quantum geometry in tellurium and related chiral materials.

item.title: Nano Letters: Resolving the Quantum Origin of Anisotropic Raman Response in Quasi-1D Ta2Ni3Te5
item.description:
Fei Wang, Qiaohui Zhou, Hong Tang, Fan Zhang, Yanxing Li, Steven A. Hindmarsh, Chengkun Xing, Keyuan Bai, et al.
Probing anisotropic electron–phonon interactions (EPIs) is fundamental to understanding low-dimensional quantum materials, yet isolating their intrinsic signatures remains a challenge due to the confounding influence of extrinsic effects. Here, we resolve this ambiguity in quasi-one-dimensional Ta2Ni3Te5 through a combination of angle-resolved polarized Raman spectroscopy and density functional perturbation theory (DFPT). Anomalous four-lobe angular dependences were observed in Ag phonon modes, which deviate from the real-valued Raman tensor prediction. Further, we explicitly highlight that, despite their distinct physical origins, light absorption and birefringence yield mathematically identical angular dependencies in Ta2Ni3Te5, rendering phenomenological fitting alone insufficient to identify the true physical mechanism. By employing a full quantum treatment incorporating detailed interaction mechanisms, we capture the qualitative characteristics and mode-to-mode diversity of the anomalous angular responses observed experimentally. The DFPT calculations further reveal mode-specific and momentum-resolved EPIs, providing microscopic support for anisotropic EPIs as the mechanism of anomalous Raman responses.

item.title: JACS: Visible-Light-Driven Dearomatization via Electrocyclic Ring Expansion for Solar Energy Storage
item.description:
Han P. Q. Nguyen, Binzhou Lin, Junichi Usuba, Subhayan Chakraborty, Abigail M. McDowell, Madeleine G. Shehadey, Grace G. D. Han
Molecular solar thermal (MOST) energy storage compounds capture solar photon energy in the strained chemical bonds of metastable photoisomers and release it on demand as heat, yet simultaneously achieving visible-light absorption and high energy storage density has remained a persistent challenge. Here we introduce 9-aryl acridine N-oxides as MOST compounds based on visible-light-driven dearomative ring expansion. Irradiation at 470 nm, near the solar irradiance maximum at 482 nm, quantitatively converts these compounds to metastable 1,2-oxazepines, which thermally revert to the parent N-oxides and discharge the stored energy. The system achieves energy storage densities of up to 0.54 MJ/kg, comparable to Dewar anthracenes, while absorbing substantially more red-shifted light and offering nearly 3 orders of magnitude longer storage lifetimes of up to 1.4 years in the solid state. The thermal half-lives of the 1,2-oxazepines are tunable through para-substitution on the aryl ring and solvation, enabling up to a 1,300-fold reduction in half-life. Crucially, the 9-aryl substituent biases the transient oxaziridine intermediate toward selective reversion to the N-oxide over competing decomposition pathways, overcoming the limitations of other acridine N-oxides reported to date. This work establishes light-induced ring expansion as an effective strategy for MOST and expands the scope of viable MOST compounds.

item.title: JACS: Conjugate Chiral Carbon Dots for Scalable Asymmetric Photocatalysis in Flow
item.description:
David M. Vahey, Dongseok Kim, Marco Bernabei, Carl J. Mallia, Erwin Reisner
Carbon dots (CDs) have emerged as scalable, metal-free photocatalysts, but their use as conjugate organo-photocatalysts for enantioselective chemistry remains unexplored. Here, we covalently anchor a chiral imidazolidinone organocatalyst to amorphous, citric acid-derived CDs, giving a colloidal conjugate that acts as both photosensitizer and enantiodetermining component. This chiral CD material promotes the asymmetric radical α-alkylation of aldehydes in up to 84% yield and 93% e.e. Its semihomogeneous nature enables catalyst recovery by precipitation and reuse over five cycles with only minor loss in yield and e.e. The well-dispersed conjugate is also compatible with continuous photoflow, where Bayesian optimization in only 10 experiments enabled a gram-scale reaction in 80% yield and 91% e.e. This work establishes chiral conjugate CDs as a practical, recoverable platform for sustainable asymmetric photocatalysis.

item.title: JACS: A Molybdoenzyme Mediates Carbon–Sulfur Bond Making and Breaking in Ergothioneine Biosynthesis
item.description:
Gladwin Suryatin Alim, Roman P. Jakob, Seseg B. Bolotova, Jing Yang, Martin L. Kirk, Timm Maier, Florian P. Seebeck
The molybdopterin-dependent ergothioneine synthase (MES) from Caldithrix abyssi is the first molybdoenzyme known to catalyze the formation of carbon–sulfur bonds. To complete its catalytic cycle, this bifunctional enzyme desulfurates l-cysteine at a pyridoxal 5′-phosphate binding site and transfers the harvested sulfur atom (S0) to the molybdenum center of a bis-molybdopterin guanine dinucleotide cofactor more than 50 Å away. Subsequently, the sulfurated Mo-center transfers the labile sulfur atom onto the imidazole ring of Nα-trimethyl histidine (TMH). Combining experimental observations from cryo-electron microscopy, X-ray crystallography, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, sequence-activity correlation, and substrate-specificity studies, we delineate the structural basis for long-distance sulfur transfer via a persulfide relay, the identity of the imidazole sulfurating species, and key sequence motifs that are indispensable for activity. Furthermore, the reversibility of MES-mediated sulfurization of TMH under physiological conditions suggests that ergothioneine may serve as a soluble reservoir of oxidizing equivalents, supporting anaerobic metabolism in deep-branching bacteria such as C. abyssi.

item.title: Nano Letters: Exciton Transport in Disordered Perovskite Nanocrystal Solids
item.description:
Simon F. Solari, Enrique Arévalo Rodríguez, Antonella Cutrupi, Amalia Coro, Marc Meléndez, Víctor Zamora, Federico J. Mompean, Alicia De Andrés, et al.
Solution-processed thin films of colloidal lead halide perovskite (LHP) nanocrystals (NCs) show great potential for next-generation optoelectronic devices. However, these NC solids exhibit non-negligible size and shape polydispersity, which introduces both structural and energetic disorder. Here we resolve the exciton dynamics in space, time, and energy to elucidate the impact of disorder on exciton transport. We show that the disorder depends sensitively on the alkylamine ligand used in the synthesis. While shorter alkyl chain lengths lead to high polydispersity, longer alkyl chains lead to a narrower size distribution and smaller particles where quantum confinement becomes more pronounced, consequently leading to increased energetic disorder. Strikingly, we find that exciton transport is less efficient in NC solids with long alkyl chains, despite the fact that they have significantly more narrowly size-distributed ensembles. This demonstrates that energetic disorder rather than structural disorder is the dominant factor for predicting exciton transport within these disordered systems.

item.title: JACS: All-Visible Wavelength-Gated Multistate Photochromic AIEgen: High-Efficiency Photocyclizations in a Single Luminogenic System
item.description:
Xinyuan He, Jinghong Shi, Wei Wen, Ryan T. K. Kwok, Jianwei Sun, Jacky W. Y. Lam, Lianrui Hu, Ben Zhong Tang
Synthetic photochromic molecules that enable noninvasive orthogonal control using distinct wavelengths of light are still in their infancy, yet ensuring the independence of photoreaction pathways and multiple addressable states in a single luminogenic system remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report an aggregation-induced emission (AIE) luminogen capable of undergoing wavelength-selective photocyclizations under visible-light irradiation, exhibiting a photorearrangement at 410 nm purple light and an oxidative photocyclization at 465 nm blue light to yield two stable yet distinct photochromic states. Experimental and theoretical results provide insight into the wavelength-dependent reaction pathways, as well as the corresponding synergistic mechanism of aromaticity, steric strain, and inductive effect in its photocyclizations. Eventually, a model information encryption system was developed to showcase its practical potential for all-visible-light-controlled multistate operations. This work thus offers both a viable strategy and a versatile structural motif for developing visible-light-controlled multistate luminogens and advanced multifunctional systems.

item.title: Nano Letters: Magnetic Exciton-Based On-Chip Optical Attenuators Using CrSBr
item.description:
Ahmet Kemal Demir, Luca Nessi, Sachin Vaidya, Marin Soljačić, Riccardo Comin
Two-dimensional magnetic semiconductors, in which excitonic resonances are coupled directly to the underlying spin order, offer a fundamentally distinct route to active photonic functionality unattainable in conventional dielectrics. The van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr exemplifies this class: its sharp excitons exhibit large oscillator strengths and energies that are continuously and reversibly tunable through the magnetic state of the material, producing dramatic field-induced changes in the permittivity. Here, we exploit this magneto-excitonic response to realize compact, magnetically tunable optical attenuators in standard silicon nitride waveguides. We demonstrate up to 2.5 dB/μm continuous attenuation from CrSBr flakes under in-plane magnetic fields below 1 T. We further show that the device response depends nontrivially on the CrSBr thickness through coupled-mode physics with the polarity of the field response inverting between the perturbative and strongly coupled regimes. This work highlights two-dimensional magnetic semiconductors as a promising materials platform for compact, continuously reconfigurable control of guided light.

item.title: ACS Nano: Janus Biofuel Cells for Electrosynergistic Enhancement of Microenvironment-Adaptive Cascade Catalysis in Infected Diabetic Wound Healing
item.description:
Guiyuan Zhang, Tianyu Gao, Shuying Ren, Junwu Wei, Xiangling Pu, Qiang Wu, Xiaohong Li
The treatment of infectious diabetic wound is greatly hampered by hyperglycemia, inflammation, and microcirculatory dysfunction. Bioelectric stimulation and nanozyme catalysis provide a potential strategy for chronic wound repair but suffer from limitations including external electric power, low activity, and competitive multienzyme reactions. Given this, we developed microenvironment-responsive Janus GOx-Au@PCH–Pt nanoparticles (NPs) as biofuel cells, integrating cascade enzymatic catalysis and self-powered electrical stimulation. The biofuel cell features hydroxylated polyaniline (PCH) NPs as conductive bridges, Pt nanoclusters as the cathode, and glucose oxidase (GOx)-grafted Au (GOx-Au) as the anode. Under infection (acidic pH), conductive PCH shuttles electrons to generate microcurrent that accelerates enzyme catalysis on both the Au anode (GOx) and Pt cathode (peroxidase, POD). The enhanced GOx-POD cascade strengthens ·OH generation, and the self-powered electric field enhances ·OH diffusion across phospholipid bilayers, achieving significant bacterial killing and biofilm dispersion. During tissue repair, neutral/alkaline conditions switch Pt nanozyme from POD to catalase (CAT) and transform PCH into a benzoquinone structure as the electron acceptor. Reversed electron flow boosts the GOx-CAT cascade catalysis on the electrodes, accelerating glucose consumption, suppressing advanced glycation end product formation, and alleviating oxidative stress, while electrical stimulation reduces hypoxia-inducible factor-1α expressions. This synergistic effect promotes collagen deposition and orderly arrangement and normalizes microenvironment with oxygen-generating, hypoglycemic, anti-inflammatory, and macrophage phenotype-shifted features, thereby accelerating wound healing. This designed nanoscale biofuel cells realize adaptive microcurrent modulation and spatiotemporal cascade catalysis, offering a minimally invasive paradigm for infected diabetic wound therapy.

item.title: ACS Nano: Nontrivial Edge Superconductivity in Dirac Superconductor PdTe2
item.description:
Bicong Ye, Zegang Liu, Tianyu Liu, Pingbo Chen, Jinhua Wang, Liang Zhou, Peiyao Qin, Hu Xu, et al.
Superconducting topological materials with coexisted superconductivities and topological boundary states are promising platforms for realizing intrinsic topological superconductivity. In this work, the superconducting type-II Dirac semimetal PdTe2 is shown to exhibit clear periodic critical current oscillations in perpendicular magnetic fields due to the fluxoid quantization, indicating the existence of edge superconductivity in PdTe2. Furthermore, a comparative study of the different superconducting properties of the bulk and edge of PdTe2 provides direct evidence for this edge superconductivity. More importantly, by a careful analysis of the flux penetration area, the nontrivial character of the edge superconductivity is revealed, i.e., the edge superconductivity appears not only at the physical boundary of the flake, but also at the interior interface between superconducting and normal regions of PdTe2. The emergence of nontrivial edge superconductivity, indicative of the putative bulk topological superconductivity, not only reveals the great potential of PdTe2 but also provides an experimental avenue for exploring intrinsic topological superconductivity by leveraging bulk-boundary correspondence.

item.title: ACS Nano: Receptor-Modular Nanocaptors for Programmable Cytokine Sequestration
item.description:
Yin-Yi Cai, Dong-Kun Zhao, Qi-Wen Fu, Long Zhu, Yu-Xin Qing, Yi-Lin Liu, Xin Li, Jing-Yuan Tian, et al.
Pathological cytokine networks underlie inflammatory injury and tumor-associated immunosuppression, yet most cytokine-targeted therapies rely on molecularly fixed, pathway-specific antagonists. We present a receptor-modular nanomaterial strategy for constructing modular cytokine nanocaptors (MCNs) whose sequestration profiles can be reconfigured by exchanging receptor modules. Cytokine receptor ectodomains are engineered as independently producible serum albumin fusion proteins and coassembled with poly(L-lactic acid) (PLLA) into compositionally defined nanoparticles. This architecture decouples cytokine-binding specificity from nanoparticle structure, enabling high-density codisplay of multiple receptor modules on single particles. Representative MCNs simultaneously sequester IL-6, TNF-α, and IFN-γ and suppress cytokine-driven inflammatory signaling more effectively than matched soluble receptor mixtures. By altering module composition while preserving the same assembly framework, MCNs can be redirected from sequestering pro-inflammatory cytokines in sepsis, acute lung injury, and fulminant hepatitis to depleting immunosuppressive mediators in tumors. These results establish receptor-modular nanocaptors as programmable materials for disease-tailored cytokine sequestration and immune-microenvironment reconfiguration.

item.title: ACS Nano: Cucurbit[ n ]uril-Programmed Chlorogenic Acid Release for Collagen Mineralization and Pulp–Dentin Repair in Near-Pulp Bonding
item.description:
Haotian Dong, Wenhui Wang, Shujing Wang, Suqing Tu, Xinyu Yang, Ran You, Haifeng Xie, Chen Chen
Long-term failure of resin–dentin bonding arises from persistent hydration and enzymatic degradation of exposed collagen in the deep hybrid layer, whereas diffusion of bioactive components through dentinal tubules toward the pulp may cause pulpal irritation. An ideal pretreatment should therefore promote collagen remineralization and interfacial stabilization while reducing pulp-adjacent cellular irritation and supporting pulp–dentin repair. Herein, supramolecular complexes of chlorogenic acid (CGA) and cucurbit[n]uril (Q[n], n = 6, 7, and 8), denoted CGA@Q[n], were constructed to regulate CGA loading, release, and interfacial exposure. CGA@Q[6] showed limited loading, release, and mineralization capacity. CGA@Q[7] exhibited faster early release and achieved complete collagen mineralization within 24 h, whereas CGA@Q[8] showed the highest encapsulation efficiency, sustained CGA supply, complete mineralization at 36 h, and a continuous, dense, integrated intrafibrillar mineral phase.
